content.title: About
content.content: Greek yogurt is a thick, creamy yogurt made by straining regular yogurt to remove whey. This version is produced from whole milk, giving it a richer flavor and higher fat content. It contains no added flavors, sweeteners, or colorants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt originates from Greece, where it is known as “strained yogurt.”
Straining boosts protein content to about 10‑12 g per 100 g serving.
Using whole milk creates a creamier texture and milder taste compared with low‑fat versions.
It is a staple in Mediterranean cuisine, often used as a base for sauces, dips, and desserts.
Unlike regular yogurt, Greek yogurt can stay fresh longer without quality loss.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The abundant protein supports muscle growth, repair, and promotes satiety.

items.title: Probiotic source
items.content: Live cultures help maintain gut health and boost the immune system.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Whole milk provides calcium and vitamin D essential for bone health.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: The fat from whole milk contains conjugated linoleic acid (CLA), which may aid metabolism.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: Unsweetened Greek yogurt contains little sugar, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort, although some lactose is removed during straining.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Whole‑milk yogurt is more calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Casein and whey proteins can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Greek yogurt can be enjoyed plain, blended into smoothies, used as a base for sauces, dressings, and dips, or incorporated into baked goods and desserts. It pairs well with berries, nuts, honey, or fresh fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the yogurt refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in its original container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not leave it at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
